title: Pseudo Timelines, Gutters, Hyphens, Commits & Close Requests
description: Five platform features that take back work you were doing by hand — from animating ::before to guarding every way a modal can close.

drops.title: Animating What Isn't There
drops.description: element.animate() takes a pseudoElement option, so ::before, ::after and ::backdrop join one scrubbable Web Animations timeline.
drops.concept: Pseudo-elements have no DOM node, so for years the only way to move them was to toggle a class and hand control to CSS. The pseudoElement option on element.animate() gives them the full Web Animations API — and Chrome 152 extended CSSPseudoElement support to ::backdrop, ::scroll-marker and view transitions. The drop runs sheens on three cards, staggered underlines on five tags and an animated dialog backdrop, all driven by one transport with play, pause, reverse, playback rate and a scrubber.
drops.source: W3C Web Animations Level 1 — the pseudoElement option

interaction.mouse: Drag the scrubber to scrape every pseudo-element animation across its timeline at once.
interaction.click: Play, pause, reverse or halve the rate of all pseudo animations; open the dialog to animate its ::backdrop.
interaction.touch: All transport controls and the parameter panel are tap-sized; the panel stacks inline on narrow screens.

drops.title: Room Reserved for the Scrollbar
drops.description: Three panes — auto, stable, and stable both-edges — reflow side by side as content crosses the overflow threshold.
drops.concept: A classic scrollbar is laid out inside the element, so the moment content stops overflowing it disappears and every line rewraps. scrollbar-gutter: stable reserves that strip whether or not the bar is showing, and both-edges mirrors it so a centred heading stays centred. The drop measures each pane's live content width, draws a centre guide, and detects overlay scrollbars honestly instead of pretending the effect is visible everywhere.

interaction.mouse: Scroll each pane to feel the reserved gutter; resize the window to re-measure.
interaction.click: Toggle the content between overflowing and short, or fire six rapid flips to watch the jump.
interaction.touch: Panes scroll with a finger; the parameter panel moves inline under the demo on phones.

drops.title: Hyphens With House Rules
drops.description: Sliders for hyphenate-limit-chars and a picker for hyphenate-character, across English, German and soft-hyphen columns.
drops.concept: Justified text in a narrow measure needs hyphenation, but left alone the engine will strand two letters on a line and stack hyphen ladders. hyphenate-limit-chars sets the minimum word length plus the characters that must survive on each side of the break, and hyphenate-character decides what the break mark looks like. Three columns compare an English dictionary, a German one, and hand-placed soft hyphens — with a live line count and an honest probe for browsers that ship no dictionary.
drops.source: Richard Rutter — All you need to know about hyphenation in CSS

interaction.mouse: Drag the three limit sliders and the column-width slider to re-break every paragraph live.
interaction.click: Switch between hyphens auto, manual and none, or change the hyphenation character.
interaction.touch: Sliders and the mode switch are full-width on phones; the panel stacks under the columns.

drops.title: Let the Fling Keep Its Place
drops.description: Drag chips, release them into a momentum fling, and commitStyles() writes the landing spot onto the element so nothing snaps back.
drops.concept: Ending a drag with a Web Animations fling has a classic tail: cancel the animation and the element jumps back to its stylesheet position; leave fill:'forwards' on and the animation outranks every later style change. commitStyles() writes the computed end state to the element's own style attribute so you can cancel cleanly. The drop pits a committed chip against an uncommitted one, adds a row of switch knobs that commit their travel, and exposes duration, momentum and easing.

interaction.mouse: Drag any chip and flick it — release speed becomes momentum, and the chip settles where it lands.
interaction.click: Fling both comparison chips at once, toggle the switch knobs, or disarm commitStyles to see the snap-back.
interaction.touch: Pointer Events cover touch dragging; the tracks and knobs are sized for thumbs.

drops.title: The Modal That Can Say No
drops.description: requestClose() fires the same cancelable event Escape does, so one guard covers Esc, light dismiss, the back gesture and your Cancel button.
drops.concept: dialog.close() is unconditional — it tears the dialog down and no listener gets a say. requestClose() instead routes through the cancelable cancel event, which means the unsaved-changes guard you wrote for the Escape key now also catches your own buttons. Three dialogs share one handler: a dirty draft, a destructive confirm that refuses until the name matches, and an unguarded dialog for contrast, with a live log of every close request and its return value.
drops.source: Manuel Matuzović — Close requests, close watchers, and the dialog element

interaction.mouse: Click the backdrop to light-dismiss and watch the guard intercept it.
interaction.click: Compare requestClose() against close() on the same dialog; switch the closedby value in the panel.
interaction.touch: Dialogs are full-width on phones and every control is tap-sized.
